title: Stop That Pawn: Promotion Skewers
summary: Promote into a checking skewer instead of judging the race only by who gets a queen first.

nodes.question: Which checking line will expose the new queen?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Kxf3 with White Kf8 and b7 against Kf3 and pawns a5, d7, d6 and h2. Both sides are about to promote.

nodes.question: What changes when the king stands on d1?
nodes.explanation: This separate source diagram already has White Qb8. Black is to move with Kd1 and h2. The king and promotion square can be attacked along the first rank.

branches.title: Use the b7–h1 diagonal
commentary: Begin after ...Kxf3 with White Kf8 and b7 against Kf3 and pawns a5, d7, d6 and h2. Both sides are about to promote.
b8=Q creates the queen needed for a checking skewer. White has not lost merely because Black also promotes.
h1=Q creates the second queen, but Kf3 stands on the b7–h1 diagonal.
Qb7+ checks along b7-c6-d5-e4-f3-g2-h1. The king is in front of its own queen.
Kg3 escapes the diagonal and exposes Qh1. This is the illustrated source reply.
Qxh1 captures the exposed queen. The exact queen-versus-three-pawns ending is winning for White.
branches.explanation: Qxh1 captures the exposed queen. The exact queen-versus-three-pawns ending is winning for White.

branches.title: Use the first rank with the king on d1
commentary: Begin in the separately pictured Qb8/Kd1 diagram, with Black to move.
h1=Q promotes, but places the queen behind Kd1 on the first rank.
Qb1+ checks Kd1 and attacks the new queen through the king.
Ke2 is a legal representative king flight from the rank check, independently supplied rather than claiming an exact sampled source move.
Qxh1 wins the queen after the king vacates the first rank. The exact remaining ending is winning for White.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Qxh1 wins the queen after the king vacates the first rank. The exact remaining ending is winning for White.

branches.title: Copy the rank idea with the king on f3
commentary: Begin after ...Kxf3 with White Kf8 and b7 against Kf3 and pawns a5, d7, d6 and h2. Both sides are about to promote.
b8=Q begins the same promotion race.
Qb1 does not check Kf3. The first-rank skewer from the Kd1 diagram does not transfer to this position.
Qxb1 captures White’s undefended queen. This independent error comparison is losing for White; geometry, not the shared promotion race, determines the right check.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Qxb1 captures White’s undefended queen. This independent error comparison is losing for White; geometry, not the shared promotion race, determines the right check.

exercises.prompt: Why is Qb7+ stronger than copying Qb1?
exercises.answer: Qb7 checks the king on f3 while lining up its queen on h1. Qb1 does not check that king and simply allows Qxb1.

startContext: Begin in the seven-piece diagram after ...Kxf3 at 94s and compare the separately pictured Qb8/Kd1 ending. The earlier knight and bishop sacrifices occur in larger setups and are source context. The diagonal skewer is illustrated; the alternative king flight and wrong-alignment comparison are independently selected legal replies.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
